title: Full reach at the sides that are not powers of two
claim: Proved: if every ring contains a contact whose basis vector is cyclic for A, full reach holds (Proposition 5; in particular a cyclic corner contact makes every contact read every corner ring). Computed, exact: the criterion holds among sides 3 to 26 exactly at 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 18, 19, 21, 23, 25, and no basis vector is cyclic at 4, 8, 14, 16, 20, 24; the census B2, every side from 3 to 130 (the powers of two run over a verified period): full reach fails exactly at 8, 16, 32, 64 and 128, where exactly n - 4 contacts miss a ring, the quarter-turn images of (X, X + 1), X = n + 2, n + 6, ..., 2n - 6, each missing one corner ring and its two neighbours, and 3n + 20 contacts miss some contact, as predicted before the run. The registered target B1, full reach at every other side, is not proved for any infinite family.
failure_conditions: A side from 3 to 130, not 8, 16, 32, 64 or 128, where some contact misses a ring.
At 128, a failing set other than the predicted 124 contacts.
foundation_claim_scope: The square torus of rule-60 rings with equally spaced law-(12, 12) contacts, cut open by a ring of cuts each way (A30, A32, A37, A38); its walk over GF(2). Reach is a contact-level reading, so it does not depend on how the rings are declared beyond which contacts each ring holds (A45).
